newsitem.title: USA: Rain stalls W. Corn Belt harvest, ice hampers hogs.
newsitem.headline: Rain stalls W. Corn Belt harvest, ice hampers hogs.

text.p: Weekend rains should keep farmers from harvesting in parts of the western Corn Belt for much of this week while cold, icy conditions may slow livestock movement in northwestern regions.

Rainfall totalled 0.75 to 2.50 inches in the western belt, locally heavier, and some snow was reported in eastern South Dakota and western Minnesota, said Joel Burgio, agricultural meteorologist with Weather Services Corp.
"In the western belt they (farmers) will be out of the fields for a few days. In the eastern belt rainfall was lighter and there won't be much delay there," he said.
Burgio said rainfall in Illinois over the weekend totalled 0.20 to 0.50 inch, while in Indiana, Ohio and Michigan it was less than 0.30 inch.
He noted that there had been little precipitation in the western belt during the last 12 hours and major roads should be clear of snow and ice.
Some livestock dealers, however, reported problems moving cattle and hogs along side roads, which remained icy.
"Hog movement will definitely be hampered on Monday by icy roads in northwestern Iowa, southeastern South Dakota and southwestern Minnesota," a Sioux Falls livestock broker said.
Meteorologists said the forecast suggested little further precipitation in the Corn Belt during the next few days.

"We did have heavy rain over the weekend in western Iowa and surrounding areas which will keep farmers out of the fields for quite a while," said Craig Solberg, meteorologist with Freese-Notis Weather.
He noted, however, that he was "not looking for a lot of precipitation during the next week to 10 days.
WSC's Burgio also said there was not much precipitation in the forecast for most of the Corn Belt between today (Monday) and Saturday.
